Paragraph: abstract

formalizesLean-only definitionsgraphee48dabf1c83d2ea

Lean proves the two claims of the first two sentences; the remaining sentences outline Sections 3 to 6 and are mapped there.

Abstract. We prove that over a Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic zero An(k)A_n(k)An​(k), every nonzero d∈An(k)d\in A_n(k)d∈An​(k) admits F,R,S∈An(k)F,R,S\in A_n(k)F,R,S∈An​(k) such that 1=dR+FdS1=dR+FdS1=dR+FdS, a conjecture Stafford proposed in 1978. As a consequence, every finitely generated torsion right An(k)A_n(k)An​(k)-module is cyclic. The proof maps ddd, by a symplectic change of variables, to a normal form d~\tilde dd~ and shows that the cyclic module Q=An(k)/(d~An(k)+x1Nd~An(k))Q=A_n(k)/(\tilde dA_n(k)+x_1^N\tilde dA_n(k))Q=An​(k)/(d~An​(k)+x1N​d~An​(k)) vanishes. We first show that right multiplication by x1x_1x1​ is surjective on QQQ. A comparison of lengths of localized modules over the associated graded ring then gives gr⁡Q=x1gr⁡Q\operatorname{gr}Q=x_1\operatorname{gr}QgrQ=x1​grQ, so that the characteristic variety of QQQ is disjoint from the hyperplane {x1=0}\{x_1=0\}{x1​=0}. Finally, Gabber's involutivity theorem together with an argument about conormal directions at infinity from algebraic geometry shows that such a characteristic variety must be empty and therefore, Q=0Q = 0Q=0.

/-- Every element of a right module is killed by some nonzero right scalar. -/
def IsRightTorsion {A : Type u} {M : Type v} [Ring A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module Aᵐᵒᵖ M] : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, ∃ d : A, d ≠ 0 ∧ (MulOpposite.op d : Aᵐᵒᵖ) • m = 0
Stafford38Challenge.IsCyclicModule formalizes Definition 2.1Stafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:281
/-- A right module `M` is cyclic: `M = mA` for some `m ∈ M`. -/
def IsCyclicModule (A : Type u) (M : Type v) [Ring A] [AddCommGroup M] [Module Aᵐᵒᵖ M] :
    Prop :=
  ∃ m : M, ∀ x : M, ∃ a : A, x = MulOpposite.op a • m

1 Introduction

Paragraph: Weyl algebra

formalizesgraph4ed676950570deb9

Lean defines A_n(k) as the free algebra on x_i, ∂_i modulo the commutator relations given by the standard symplectic matrix; PresentedWeyl is the same algebra.

Let kkk be a field of characteristic zero, and let

An(k)=k⟨x1,…,xn,∂1,…,∂n⟩ A_n(k)=k\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n,\partial_1,\ldots,\partial_n\rangleAn​(k)=k⟨x1​,…,xn​,∂1​,…,∂n​⟩
be the nnnth Weyl algebra, with [∂i,xj]=δij[\partial_i,x_j]=\delta_{ij}[∂i​,xj​]=δij​ and [∂i,∂j]=[xi,xj]=0[\partial_i,\partial_j]=[x_i,x_j]=0[∂i​,∂j​]=[xi​,xj​]=0.

Paragraph: Conjecture 3.8 and stable cyclicity

formalizesgraph441f87c51dcad41c

UniversalStatement requires d ≠ 0, as the paper quotes the conjecture. The implication to stable cyclicity, which the paper attributes to Stafford, is proved in Lean (corollary_6_3_stablyCyclic, through the printed proof of Corollary 6.3), not cited.

Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 in [Stafford 1978] asks whether every nonzero d∈An(k)d\in A_n(k)d∈An​(k) admits F∈An(k)F\in A_n(k)F∈An​(k) with An(k)=dAn(k)+FdAn(k)A_n(k)=dA_n(k)+FdA_n(k)An​(k)=dAn​(k)+FdAn​(k) [Stafford 1978, p. 438]. Stafford shows that this is a formulation that implies stable cyclicity for all finitely generated torsion right Weyl-algebra modules [Stafford 1978, pp. 437–438]. We prove Stafford's conjecture:

Stafford38Challenge.PaperCorollary_6_3_stablyCyclic defStafford38/PaperClaimDefinitions.lean:31
/-- **Corollary 6.3, stable cyclicity** (tex lines 75, 108, 1619).  Every
finitely generated torsion right `A_n(k)`-module is stably cyclic. -/
def PaperCorollary_6_3_stablyCyclic : Prop :=
  ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ M] [Module.Finite (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ M],
    Stafford38.TorsionCyclicity.IsRightTorsion (A := WeylAlg k n) (M := M) →
      IsStablyCyclic (WeylAlg k n) M
Stafford38Challenge.IsStablyCyclic defStafford38/PaperClaimDefinitions.lean:20
/-- Stafford's *stably cyclic* [Sta78, p. 435], as quoted in the proof of
Corollary 6.3 (tex line 1619): "given `l ≥ 1` and `a_1, …, a_{l+1} ∈ T` that
generate `T`, there exist `f_i ∈ A_n` such that `a_i + a_{l+1} f_i`,
`i = 1, …, l`, also generate `T`". -/
def IsStablyCyclic (A : Type u) (T : Type v) [Ring A] [AddCommGroup T] [Module Aᵐᵒᵖ T] :
    Prop :=
  ∀ l ≥ 1, ∀ a : Fin (l + 1) → T, Submodule.span Aᵐᵒᵖ (Set.range a) = ⊤ →
    ∃ f : Fin l → A, Submodule.span Aᵐᵒᵖ
      (Set.range fun i : Fin l => a i.castSucc + (MulOpposite.op (f i) : Aᵐᵒᵖ) • a (Fin.last l)) =
        ⊤

Theorem 1.1

formalizesLean-only definitionsgraph8b8cd01ddd7cb333

PaperTheorem_1_1 is the printed statement: the span form, the identity form and, for n ≥ 1, F = Φ_{g⁻¹}(x₁)^{deg_B d} with g in the symplectic group (g J gᵀ = J); the moreover clause is stated in identity form. The paper-route proofs are theorem_1_1 and theorem_1_1_fixedSource (Section 6, outside this part); theorem_1_1 of the Challenge assembles them. The paper's own Lean reference below the theorem names Stafford38.universalStatement in FoundationClosure.lean, a separate assembly that does not go through Stafford38.Paper.

Theorem 1.1.

For every field of characteristic zero kkk, every n≥0n\geq0n≥0, and every nonzero d∈An(k)d\in A_n(k)d∈An​(k), there exists an F∈An(k)F\in A_n(k)F∈An​(k) such that

An(k)=dAn(k)+FdAn(k), A_n(k)=dA_n(k)+FdA_n(k),An​(k)=dAn​(k)+FdAn​(k),
or equivalenty, there exist F,S,R∈An(k)F, S, R\in A_n(k)F,S,R∈An​(k) such that
1=dR+FdS. 1=dR+FdS.1=dR+FdS.
Moreover, if n≥1n\ge1n≥1, one may choose F=Φg−1(x1)deg⁡BdF=\Phi_g^{-1}(x_1)^{\deg_Bd}F=Φg−1​(x1​)degB​d for a linear ω\omegaω-preserving automorphism ggg as in Section 3.

Stafford38Challenge.PaperTheorem_1_1 defStafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:286
/-- **Theorem 1.1.**  For every field of characteristic zero `k`, every `n ≥ 0`
and every nonzero `d ∈ A_n(k)`, there exists an `F ∈ A_n(k)` such that
`A_n(k) = dA_n(k) + FdA_n(k)`, or equivalently, there exist `F, S, R ∈ A_n(k)`
such that `1 = dR + FdS`.  Moreover, if `n ≥ 1`, one may choose
`F = Φ_g^{-1}(x₁)^{deg_B d}` for a linear `ω`-preserving automorphism `g`. -/
def PaperTheorem_1_1 : Prop :=
  ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ) (d : WeylAlg k n), d ≠ 0 →
    (∃ F : WeylAlg k n, (⊤ : Submodule (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ (WeylAlg k n)) =
        Submodule.span (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ {d} ⊔ Submodule.span (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ {F * d}) ∧
      (∃ F S R : WeylAlg k n, (1 : WeylAlg k n) = d * R + F * d * S) ∧
      (∀ hn : 1 ≤ n, ∃ g : Matrix.symplecticGroup (Fin n) k, ∃ R S : WeylAlg k n,
        (1 : WeylAlg k n) = d * R +
          phiG k n g⁻¹ (x₁ k hn) ^ Stafford38FixedSourceChallenge.bernsteinDegree k d * d * S)
Stafford38Challenge.phiG defStafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:271
/-- **`Φ_g`**: for a linear `ω`-preserving automorphism `g` of the generator
space (`g J gᵀ = J`, i.e. `g ∈ Sp(2n, k)`), the algebra automorphism of
`A_n(k)` extending `u_i ↦ g(u_i) = ∑_j g_ij u_j`.  Its inverse is
`Φ_g⁻¹ = Φ_{g⁻¹}`. -/
noncomputable def phiG (k : Type*) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (g : Matrix.symplecticGroup (Fin n) k) :
    WeylAlg k n →ₐ[k] WeylAlg k n :=
  RingQuot.liftAlgHom k
    ⟨FreeAlgebra.lift k (linearImage k (g : Matrix (PhaseVar n) (PhaseVar n) k)),
      fun _ _ h => linearImage_rel k g h⟩

Stafford38FixedSourceChallenge.UniversalFixedSourceStatementWithDegree defStafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:181
/-- Shared template for the fixed-source proposition, parameterized only by
the chosen degree function. -/
def UniversalFixedSourceStatementWithDegree
    (degree : ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] {n : ℕ}, WeylAlg k n → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ)
    (d : WeylAlg k (n + 1)), d ≠ 0 →
      ∃ ell R S : WeylAlg k (n + 1),
        IsLinearWeylCoordinate k n ell ∧
          (1 : WeylAlg k (n + 1)) =
            d * R + ell ^ degree k d * d * S

Stafford38FixedSourceChallenge.IsLinearWeylCoordinate defStafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:168
/-- A source coordinate obtained from an invertible symplectic linear change
of the canonical Weyl generators. -/
def IsLinearWeylCoordinate (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ)
    (ell : WeylAlg k (n + 1)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M N : Matrix (PhaseVar (n + 1)) (PhaseVar (n + 1)) k)
      (_hM : M * standardForm k (n + 1) * Matrix.transpose M =
        standardForm k (n + 1))
      (_hN : N * standardForm k (n + 1) * Matrix.transpose N =
        standardForm k (n + 1))
      (_hMN : M * N = 1) (_hNM : N * M = 1),
      ell = linearCombination k N (generator k (n + 1))
        (.inl (0 : Fin (n + 1)))

/-- Span of the ordered Weyl words of total degree at most `N`. -/
def bernsteinPiece (k : Type u) [Field k] (n N : ℕ) :
    Submodule k (WeylAlg k n) :=
  Submodule.span k
    {z | ∃ a p : Fin n → ℕ,
      phaseDegree a p ≤ N ∧ z = orderedMonomial k n a p}
Stafford38FixedSourceChallenge.orderedMonomial Lean onlyStafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:137
/-- The image of an ordered PBW word in the shared Weyl quotient. -/
def orderedMonomial (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ)
    (a p : Fin n → ℕ) : WeylAlg k n :=
  RingQuot.mkAlgHom k (relation (k := k) (n := n) (Matrix.J (Fin n) k))
    (freeOrderedMonomial k n a p)

/-- Total degree of a split coordinate/momentum exponent. -/
def phaseDegree {n : ℕ} (a p : Fin n → ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (∑ i, a i) + ∑ i, p i

Stafford38FixedSourceChallenge.freeOrderedMonomial Lean onlyStafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:127
/-- Ordered PBW words, with old pairs followed by the newest pair. -/
def freeOrderedMonomial (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → ℕ) → (Fin n → ℕ) → FreeAlgebra k (PhaseVar n)
  | 0, _, _ => 1
  | n + 1, a, p =>
      freeOldMap k n
          (freeOrderedMonomial k n (fun i => a i.succ) (fun i => p i.succ)) *
        FreeAlgebra.ι k (.inl (0 : Fin (n + 1))) ^ a 0 *
        FreeAlgebra.ι k (.inr (0 : Fin (n + 1))) ^ p 0

Paragraph: proof sketch

prosegraph21a1a1236a2093dd

Outline of Sections 3 to 6; each claim is mapped at the environment it summarizes.

Proof sketch: We state some preliminaries in section 2, then start in section 3 by defining a map Φg\Phi_gΦg​ sending any chosen ddd of Bernstein degree NNN to a monic normal form d~\tilde dd~ with order symbol PPP using Bernstein and order filtrations of An(k)A_n(k)An​(k). For d~\tilde dd~, we prove in sections 4-6 that the module Q=An(k)/(d~An(k)+x1Nd~An(k))=0Q = A_n(k)/(\tilde d A_n(k) + x_1^N\tilde d A_n(k)) = 0Q=An​(k)/(d~An​(k)+x1N​d~An​(k))=0, and find the final form of Theorem 1.1 by applying the inverse map Φg−1\Phi_g^{-1}Φg−1​ to d~An(k)+x1Nd~An(k).\tilde d A_n(k) + x_1^N\tilde d A_n(k).d~An​(k)+x1N​d~An​(k). The main components of the proof are the following: in section 4, we show that Q=Qx1Q = Qx_1Q=Qx1​ using the extended euclidean algorithm, and gr⁡Q=x1gr⁡Q,\gr Q = x_1\gr Q,grQ=x1​grQ, through two contradictory length estimations of localized modules. In section 5 using mainly results from algebraic geometry, we show that a set WWW fulfilling certain criteria (Zariski closed over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, fibre-conical, involutive, and there exists a polynomial with P(1,0…,0)≠0P(1,0\dots,0)\neq 0P(1,0…,0)=0 vanishing on WWW, and WWW does not contain points with x1=0x_1 = 0x1​=0) must always be empty (Theorem 5.8). Finally, we show in section 6 that by defining WWW to be the characteristic variety of the closed-field pendant to QQQ, the results of section 4 as well as the definition of PPP in section 3 ensure that WWW fulfills all criteria and must thus be empty. We conclude that therefore, also QQQ itself must be zero, from which Theorem 1.1 follows directly. Lastly, we provide the proof by Stafford [Stafford 1978] that hence, every finitely generated torsion module is stably cyclic (Corollary 6.3).

Paragraph: related literature

prosegraph47ed3cd8e4b85eee

Results of other authors, cited; not formalized here.

Related literature
Dixmier showed that over the first Weyl algebra A1(k)A_1(k)A1​(k) with kkk having characteristic zero, any right ideal can be generated by at most two elements [Dixmier 1968]. In a seminal paper in 1978, Stafford extended this result to all An(k)A_n(k)An​(k) and moreover showed, that any finitely generated left torsion An(k)A_n(k)An​(k)-module is isomorphic to a right ideal, and as such can also be (stably) generated be at most two elements [Stafford 1978, Theorem 3.7]. Hillebrand and Schmale [Hillebrand 2001], as well as Leykin [Leykin 2004] give an algorithm to find the two generators of left ideals, also valid for rational coefficient algebras Bn(k)B_n(k)Bn​(k). Caro and Lefcovitz [Caro 2010] generalize the result for both left and right ideals to formal and to convergent Laurent series, and and Quadrat and Robertz [Quadrat 2014] provide a constructive proof method to calculate the two generators of torsion modules over the Weyl algebras, as well as rings with rational coefficients, formal or convergent Laurent series, and, for ordinary differential operators with formal or locally convergent power series coefficients.

No Lean counterpart.

Paragraph: Stafford 1978

prosegraphf042561eda94903d

Report on Stafford 1978. The identification with Theorem 1.1 and the stable cyclicity are the Lean statements shown with the paragraph on Conjecture 3.8; the monomial case is an instance of Theorem 1.1 with no separate Lean statement; the case n = 1 through the restricted minimum condition is not formalized.

In the same paper, Stafford states the Conjecture 3.8, which is Theorem 1.1, and shows that this conjecture implies that any finitely generated right torsion module can be stably generated by one element, i.e. is stably cyclic (Corollary 6.3). He shows that cyclicity is true if n=1n = 1n=1 (since A1(k)A_1(k)A1​(k) has the restricted minimum condition which makes torsion modules Artinian and he proves that Artinian modules are cyclic) and also states that the conjecture is true if ddd is monomial, but provides, as far as the authors are aware, no proof of this. This case is also contained in our proof. For holonomic modules over "simple rings such that they do not have finite length over themselves as left modules" (which all Weyl algebras are), Leykin [Leykin 2004] proved cyclicity constructively, and attributed the proof method to Stafford. However, torsion modules need not be holonomic: for n≥2n\ge2n≥2, Stafford constructed quotients An(k)/dAn(k)A_n(k)/dA_n(k)An​(k)/dAn​(k) of Gelfand–Kirillov dimension 2n−12n-12n−1 as counterexamples [Stafford 1985], so the question about cyclicity remained open for non-holonomic torsion modules. A survey by Bellamy in 2026 [Bellamy 2026] states this explicitly (Conjecture 3.4).

No Lean counterpart.

Paragraph: holonomic modules

prosegraph55b8a7807bfff24f

Results of other authors, cited; not formalized here.

In the same paper, Stafford states the Conjecture 3.8, which is Theorem 1.1, and shows that this conjecture implies that any finitely generated right torsion module can be stably generated by one element, i.e. is stably cyclic (Corollary 6.3). He shows that cyclicity is true if n=1n = 1n=1 (since A1(k)A_1(k)A1​(k) has the restricted minimum condition which makes torsion modules Artinian and he proves that Artinian modules are cyclic) and also states that the conjecture is true if ddd is monomial, but provides, as far as the authors are aware, no proof of this. This case is also contained in our proof. For holonomic modules over "simple rings such that they do not have finite length over themselves as left modules" (which all Weyl algebras are), Leykin [Leykin 2004] proved cyclicity constructively, and attributed the proof method to Stafford. However, torsion modules need not be holonomic: for n≥2n\ge2n≥2, Stafford constructed quotients An(k)/dAn(k)A_n(k)/dA_n(k)An​(k)/dAn​(k) of Gelfand–Kirillov dimension 2n−12n-12n−1 as counterexamples [Stafford 1985], so the question about cyclicity remained open for non-holonomic torsion modules. A survey by Bellamy in 2026 [Bellamy 2026] states this explicitly (Conjecture 3.4).

No Lean counterpart.

We base our proof on the Weyl algebra and on filtrations and characteristic varieties of An(k)A_n(k)An​(k)-modules as treated in the textbooks [Coutinho 1995, Bj 1979, Hotta 2008, McConnell 2001, Schnell 2019]; on the involutivity of the characteristic variety due to Gabber [Gabber 1981, Gabber 1982, Singh 2014]; on commutative algebra, in particular localization, length, valuation rings, Kähler differentials and completions [Atiyah 1969, Matsumura 1986, Authors 2026], together with field theory and bilinear forms [Lang 2012] and spectral sequences [Weibel 1994]; and on algebraic geometry, mostly based on [hartshorne].

Paragraph: formal verification

prosegraphe6fa8299b10afe5a

Claims about the formalization, checked outside this view: at the pinned Lean commit, #print axioms in Solution.lean reports propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for every compared theorem, and lake-manifest.json pins AlgebraicAnalysis at its tag v0.3.3.

Formal verification with Lean
Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 6.3 are proved in Lean 4 [Moura 2021] with Mathlib [Community 2020] and AlgebraicAnalysis v0.3.3 [Albert 2026]. The proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms: propositional extensionality (propext), the axiom of choice (Classical.choice) and soundness of quotient types (Quot.sound). Every intermediate result is proved in Lean as well, including Gabber's involutivity theorem for cyclic An(k)A_n(k)An​(k)-modules. The proof in Sections 3–6 follows the formal proof step by step; where the two routes differ, the text says so. The main theorem is registered in Palomar [Albert 2026], and the Lean sources are archived [Albert]. Tooling and the role of AI assistance are described in Appendix ??app:ai-workflow. Section 7 states further consequences proved in Lean and two generalizations, to rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties and to simple filtered algebras. The supplementary material [Albert 2026] shows each formalized statement of this paper next to its Lean version and proof. It can be browsed at https://itpplasma.github.io/stafford38-supplementary/.

No Lean counterpart.

2 Preliminaries

Paragraph: right modules

prosegraph55e6bf8b6190c012

Convention. Lean writes a right A_n(k)-module as a module over A_n(k)ᵐᵒᵖ, so m·a is op a • m, and a right ideal as a submodule of the regular right module.

Throughout, kkk is a field of characteristic zero and for the nnn-th Weyl algebra over kkk, we write

An(k)=k⟨x1,…,xn,∂1,…,∂n⟩,[∂i,xj]=δij,[xi,xj]=[∂i,∂j]=0. A_n(k)=k\langle x_1,\dots,x_n,\partial_1,\dots,\partial_n\rangle, \quad [\partial_i,x_j]=\delta_{ij},\quad [x_i,x_j]=[\partial_i,\partial_j]=0 .An​(k)=k⟨x1​,…,xn​,∂1​,…,∂n​⟩,[∂i​,xj​]=δij​,[xi​,xj​]=[∂i​,∂j​]=0.
All ideals are right ideals and all modules are right modules unless the contrary is said explicitly.

No Lean counterpart.

Stafford38.Paper.Section2.IsCyclic defStafford38/Paper/Section2/Weyl.lean:44
/-- **Definition 2.1 (cyclic).** `M = mA` for some `m ∈ M`. -/
def IsCyclic : Prop :=
  ∃ m : M, ∀ x : M, ∃ a : A, x = MulOpposite.op a • m
Stafford38.TorsionCyclicity.IsRightTorsion defStafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:202
/-- Every element of a right module is killed by some nonzero right scalar. -/
def IsRightTorsion {A : Type u} {M : Type v} [Ring A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module Aᵐᵒᵖ M] : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, ∃ d : A, d ≠ 0 ∧ (MulOpposite.op d : Aᵐᵒᵖ) • m = 0
Stafford38Challenge.IsCyclicModule defStafford38/ChallengeDefinitions.lean:281
/-- A right module `M` is cyclic: `M = mA` for some `m ∈ M`. -/
def IsCyclicModule (A : Type u) (M : Type v) [Ring A] [AddCommGroup M] [Module Aᵐᵒᵖ M] :
    Prop :=
  ∃ m : M, ∀ x : M, ∃ a : A, x = MulOpposite.op a • m

/-- **Convention 2.2, relations.** `x₁` is central in `C`, `[p, x₁] = 1`, and
the transverse algebra commutes with `x₁` and `p`. -/
theorem convention_2_2_relations (n : ℕ) :
    p k n * x₁ k n = x₁ k n * p k n + 1 ∧
      (∀ c ∈ C k n, x₁ k n * c = c * x₁ k n) ∧
      ∀ t ∈ transverse k n, t * x₁ k n = x₁ k n * t ∧ t * p k n = p k n * t := by
  refine ⟨presentedMomentum_mul_coordinate k n, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro c hc
    induction hc using Algebra.adjoin_induction with
    | mem x hx =>
        rcases hx with ⟨w, rfl⟩ | hx
        · exact presentedCoordinate_commutes_previous k n w
        · rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hx]
    | algebraMap r => exact (Algebra.commutes r _).symm
    | add x y _ _ hx hy => rw [mul_add, add_mul, hx, hy]
    | mul x y _ _ hx hy => rw [← mul_assoc, hx, mul_assoc, hy, mul_assoc]
  · rintro _ ⟨w, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨(presentedCoordinate_commutes_previous k n w).symm,
      (presentedMomentum_commutes_previous k n w).symm⟩

/-- **Convention 2.2, normal form (existence).** Every element of `A_n(k)` can
be written as `∑_j p^j c_j` with `c_j ∈ C`. -/
theorem convention_2_2_exists (n : ℕ) (d : PresentedWeyl k (n + 1)) :
    ∃ (L : ℕ) (a : ℕ → PresentedWeyl k (n + 1)), (∀ j, a j ∈ C k n) ∧
      d = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, p k n ^ j * a j := by
  let b := pairStage_rightOrePBWBasis (B := IteratedPairStage k n)
  let c := b.repr (presentedToIterated k (n + 1) d)
  let L := c.support.sup id + 1
  have hsub : c.support ⊆ Finset.range L := by
    intro j hj
    exact Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_of_le (Finset.le_sup (f := id) hj))
  refine ⟨L, fun j => coordinateStageToPresented k n (c j).unop,
    fun j => (C_eq_range k n).symm ▸ ⟨_, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
  have hd : presentedToIterated k (n + 1) d =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, c j • rightPBWMonomial (coordinateDerivation :
        OreDivisionDerivation (CoordinateStage (B := IteratedPairStage k n))) j := by
    conv_lhs => rw [← b.linearCombination_repr (presentedToIterated k (n + 1) d)]
    rw [Finsupp.linearCombination_apply, Finsupp.sum_of_support_subset _ hsub _ (by simp)]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro j _
    simp [b, pairStage_rightOrePBWBasis]
    rfl
  have hback : d = stageToPresented k n (presentedToIterated k (n + 1) d) :=
    (DFunLike.congr_fun (iteratedToPresented_comp_presentedToIterated k (n + 1)) d).symm
  rw [hback, hd, map_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  exact stageToPresented_rightTerm k n j (c j).unop

/-- **Convention 2.2, normal form (uniqueness).** If `∑_{j<L} p^j c_j = 0`
with `c_j ∈ C`, then every `c_j = 0`. -/
theorem convention_2_2_unique (n L : ℕ) (a : ℕ → PresentedWeyl k (n + 1))
    (ha : ∀ j, a j ∈ C k n) (h0 : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, p k n ^ j * a j = 0) :
    ∀ j < L, a j = 0 := by
  have hpre : ∀ j, ∃ z, coordinateStageToPresented k n z = a j := fun j => by
    have := ha j
    rw [C_eq_range] at this
    exact this
  choose b hb using hpre
  let D : OreDivisionDerivation (CoordinateStage (B := IteratedPairStage k n)) :=
    coordinateDerivation
  have hsum : rightPBWCombination D
      (∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, Finsupp.single j (MulOpposite.op (b j))) = 0 := by
    rw [map_sum]
    simp only [rightPBWCombination_single]
    have himg : stageToPresented k n
        (∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, MulOpposite.op (b j) • rightPBWMonomial D j) = 0 := by
      rw [map_sum, ← h0]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      rw [stageToPresented_rightTerm, hb]
    have := congrArg (presentedToIterated k (n + 1)) himg
    rwa [presentedToIterated_stageToPresented, map_zero] at this
  have hzero := (rightPBWCombination_injective D) (hsum.trans (map_zero _).symm)
  intro j hj
  have hj' := congrArg (fun f : ℕ →₀ (CoordinateStage (B := IteratedPairStage k n))ᵐᵒᵖ => f j)
    hzero
  simp only [Finsupp.coe_finsetSum, Finset.sum_apply, Finsupp.single_apply,
    Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_range, ite_eq_left hj, Finsupp.coe_zero, Pi.zero_apply] at hj'
  rw [← hb, MulOpposite.op_injective (hj'.trans MulOpposite.op_zero.symm), map_zero]

    (oldGenerator_commutator k n)

Definition 2.3 ([Def. 2.6 and  2.9 [Schnell 2019]]).

A filtration F∙F_\bulletF∙​ on An(k)A_n(k)An​(k) is a sequence of linear subspaces

{0}=F−1⊆F0⊆F1⊆...⊆An(k),\{0\} = F_{-1} \subseteq F_0 \subseteq F_1\subseteq...\subseteq A_n(k),{0}=F−1​⊆F0​⊆F1​⊆...⊆An​(k),
such that Fi⋅Fj⊆Fi+jF_i\cdot F_j \subseteq F_{i+j}Fi​⋅Fj​⊆Fi+j​ and An(k)=⋃Fj.A_n(k) = \bigcup F_j.An​(k)=⋃Fj​. The associated graded algebra, also called symbol ring, is defined as
grFAn(k)=⨁j=0∞Fj/Fj−1.\mathrm{gr}^F A_n(k) = \bigoplus_{j = 0}^\infty F_j/F_{j-1}.grFAn​(k)=j=0⨁∞​Fj​/Fj−1​.
Let a≠0∈An(k)a\neq 0 \in A_n(k)a=0∈An​(k) and let jjj be the smallest integer, such that a∈Fja \in F_ja∈Fj​, called a filtration degree deg⁡Fa\deg_F adegF​a. The class of aaa in Fj/Fj−1F_j/F_{j-1}Fj​/Fj−1​ is called its symbol σj(a)\sigma_j(a)σj​(a). A symbol, being the class of an element in a single graded piece, is automatically homogeneous of the corresponding degree, i.e. contains only terms of that total degree.

Stafford38.Paper.Section2.IsFiltration structureStafford38/Paper/Section2/Filtration.lean:77
/-- **Definition 2.3 (filtration).** `F_0 ⊆ F_1 ⊆ … ⊆ A` linear subspaces with
`F_i F_j ⊆ F_{i+j}` and `A = ⋃_j F_j`. -/
structure IsFiltration (F : ℕ → Submodule k A) : Prop where
  mono : Monotone F
  mul_mem : ∀ {i j : ℕ} {a b : A}, a ∈ F i → b ∈ F j → a * b ∈ F (i + j)
  exhaustive : ∀ a : A, ∃ j, a ∈ F j
Stafford38.Paper.Section2.gr defStafford38/Paper/Section2/Filtration.lean:65
/-- **Definition 2.3 (associated graded).** `gr^F = ⊕_{j ≥ 0} F_j/F_{j-1}`
as a `k`-module, for a filtration of an algebra or (Definition 2.4) of a
module. -/
abbrev gr (F : ℕ → Submodule k M) :=
  DirectSum ℕ (grPiece F)
Stafford38.Paper.Section2.filtrationDegree defStafford38/Paper/Section2/Filtration.lean:84
/-- **Definition 2.3 (filtration degree).** `deg_F a` is the smallest `j` with
`a ∈ F_j`. -/
def filtrationDegree (F : ℕ → Submodule k A) (a : A) : ℕ :=
  sInf {j | a ∈ F j}
Stafford38.Paper.Section2.symbol defStafford38/Paper/Section2/Filtration.lean:93
/-- **Definition 2.3 (symbol).** `σ_j(a)` is the class of `a` in `F_j/F_{j-1}`
for `j = deg_F a`. -/
def symbol {F : ℕ → Submodule k A} (hF : IsFiltration F) (a : A) :
    grPiece F (filtrationDegree F a) :=
  Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨a, mem_filtrationDegree hF a⟩

Paragraph: Bernstein and order filtrations

formalizesLean-only definitionsgraph4573153fce6ec3de

Lean defines both filtrations as spans of ordered PBW words of bounded weight and proves gr A_n(k) ≅ k[x, ξ] (cited by the paper).

In the proof, we use two filtrations of An(k)A_n(k)An​(k) (for more details, see e.g. [Coutinho 1995, Chapter 7])

  • The Bernstein filtration B∙B_\bulletB∙​ assigns degree 111 to every xix_ixi​ and every ∂i\partial_i∂i​. The Bernstein degree of ddd is written deg⁡Bd\deg_B ddegB​d.
  • The order filtration F∙F_\bulletF∙​ assigns degree 000 to every xix_ixi​ and degree 111 to every ∂i\partial_i∂i​; FmF_mFm​ is spanned by the monomials xα∂βx^\alpha\partial^\betaxα∂β with ∣β∣≤m|\beta|\le m∣β∣≤m.
Lean (as spans of ordered PBW words of bounded weight): Stafford38.WeylFiltration.bernsteinPiece, Stafford38.WeylFiltration.orderPiece, Stafford38.FixedSource.bernsteinDegree For both the order filtration and the Bernstein filtration, the associated graded algebra grAn(k)\mathrm{gr} A_n(k)grAn​(k) is simply the polynomial ring k[x,ξ]=k[x1,…,xn,ξ1,…,ξn]k[x,\xi]=k[x_1,\dots,x_n,\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n]k[x,ξ]=k[x1​,…,xn​,ξ1​,…,ξn​] in 2n2n2n variables with ξi\xi_iξi​ the symbol of ∂i\partial_i∂i​ [Coutinho 1995, Th. 7.3.1]. In particular, grAn(k)\mathrm{gr} A_n(k)grAn​(k) is commutative [Schnell 2019, Prop. 2.10]. Good filtrations and characteristic varieties are treated systematically for example in [Bj 1979, Hotta 2008].

  bernsteinPiece k n

Stafford38.Paper.Section2.grEquivSymbolRing defStafford38/Paper/Section2/Filtration.lean:179
/-- **`gr A_n(k) = k[x, ξ]`** for the Bernstein and the order filtration
(any weight): `⊕_j F_j/F_{j-1}` is identified with the polynomial ring by
summing the homogeneous symbols.  Multiplication of classes is the product of
symbols, `σ_{i+j}(ab) = σ_i(a)σ_j(b)`
(`WeylLeadingSymbol.presentedPrincipalComponent_mul_bernstein`,
`presentedPrincipalComponent_mul_order`), so `gr A_n(k)` is commutative. -/
def grEquivSymbolRing {n : ℕ} (w : PhaseVar n → ℕ) :
    gr (presentedWeightPiece k w) ≃ₗ[k] SymbolRing k n := by
  letI := MvPolynomial.weightedDecomposition k w
  exact (DFinsupp.mapRange.linearEquiv fun j => grPieceEquiv k w j).trans
    (DirectSum.decomposeLinearEquiv (MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousSubmodule k w)).symm

/-- Symbols supported on monomials of weighted degree at most `N`. -/
def symbolWeightPiece {n : ℕ} (w : PhaseVar n → ℕ) (N : ℕ) :
    Submodule k (SymbolRing k n) where
  carrier := {f | ∀ m, MvPolynomial.coeff m f ≠ 0 → monomialWeight w m ≤ N}
  zero_mem' m hm := by simp at hm
  add_mem' {f g} hf hg m hm := by
    by_cases hfm : MvPolynomial.coeff m f = 0
    · apply hg m
      simpa [MvPolynomial.coeff_add, hfm] using hm
    · exact hf m hfm
  smul_mem' c f hf m hm := by
    apply hf m
    intro hfm
    apply hm
    simp [MvPolynomial.coeff_smul, hfm]

/-- Normal-form coordinates for the quotient presentation, obtained by

def presentedNormalFormLinearEquiv (n : Nat) :

Stafford38.WeylPBW.iteratedNormalFormLinearEquiv Lean onlyStafford38/Weyl/PBW.lean:233
/-- Scalar-linear normal-form coordinates for the recursively iterated Ore
tower. -/
def iteratedNormalFormLinearEquiv :
    (n : Nat) → IteratedPairStage k n ≃ₗ[k] SymbolRing k n
  | 0 => (MvPolynomial.isEmptyAlgEquiv k (PhaseVar 0)).symm.toLinearEquiv
  | n + 1 => by
      letI : Algebra k (IteratedPairStage k n) :=
        iteratedPairStageAlgebra k n
      letI : Algebra k (CoordinateStage (B := IteratedPairStage k n)) :=
        coordinateStageAlgebra
      letI : Algebra k (PairStage (B := IteratedPairStage k n)) :=
        pairStageAlgebra
      change PairStage (B := IteratedPairStage k n) ≃ₗ[k] SymbolRing k (n + 1)
      exact (pairNormalFormLinearEquiv
        (normalOreAlgebra_algebraMap zeroDerivation (fun c => by
          exact zeroDerivation_apply (algebraMap k (IteratedPairStage k n) c)))
        (normalOreAlgebra_algebraMap coordinateDerivation
          coordinateDerivation_algebraMap)
        (iteratedNormalFormLinearEquiv n)).trans (flattenPairSymbols k n)

/-- Flatten the two new univariate normal-form layers and the old symbol
coefficients into the standard rank-successor symbol ring. -/
def flattenPairSymbols (n : Nat) :
    Polynomial (Polynomial (SymbolRing k n)) ≃ₗ[k] SymbolRing k (n + 1) :=
  (nestedPolynomialLinearEquiv.{u, u}
      (k := k) (R := SymbolRing k n)).trans
    ((((MvPolynomial.sumAlgEquiv k (PUnit.{1} ⊕ PUnit.{1}) (PhaseVar n)).symm
      ).toLinearEquiv).trans
        (MvPolynomial.renameEquiv k (phaseSuccEquiv n)).toLinearEquiv)
Stafford38.WeylPBW.phaseSuccEquiv Lean onlyStafford38/Weyl/PBW.lean:42
/-- Reindex the two newest symbol variables followed by the old variables to
the standard newest-first coordinate/momentum indexing. -/
def phaseSuccEquiv (n : Nat) :
    ((PUnit.{1} ⊕ PUnit.{1}) ⊕ PhaseVar n) ≃ PhaseVar (n + 1) where
  toFun
    | .inl (.inl _) => .inr 0
    | .inl (.inr _) => .inl 0
    | .inr (.inl i) => .inl i.succ
    | .inr (.inr i) => .inr i.succ
  invFun
    | .inl i => Fin.cases (.inl (.inr PUnit.unit))
        (fun j => .inr (.inl j)) i
    | .inr i => Fin.cases (.inl (.inl PUnit.unit))
        (fun j => .inr (.inr j)) i
  left_inv x := by
    rcases x with (⟨⟨u⟩ | ⟨u⟩⟩ | ⟨i | i⟩) <;> rfl
  right_inv x := by
    rcases x with (i | i)
    · exact Fin.cases rfl (fun _ => rfl) i
    · exact Fin.cases rfl (fun _ => rfl) i

/-- The central-coordinate extension of `B`. -/
abbrev CoordinateStage := NormalOre (zeroDerivation : OreDivisionDerivation B)
Stafford38.OreCoordinateStage.coordinateDerivation Lean onlyStafford38/Ore/CoordinateStage.lean:87
/-- Ordinary polynomial differentiation, transported to the central Ore
stage. -/
def coordinateDerivation : OreDivisionDerivation (CoordinateStage (B := B)) where
  toFun z := normalForm zeroDerivation
    (Polynomial.derivative ((normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm z))
  map_zero' := by
    change normalForm zeroDerivation
      (Polynomial.derivative ((normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm 0)) = 0
    rw [(normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm.map_zero,
      Polynomial.derivative_zero, normalForm_zero]
  map_add' z w := by
    have h := (normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm.toAddHom.map_add z w
    change (normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm (z + w) =
      (normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm z +
        (normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm w at h
    change normalForm zeroDerivation
      (Polynomial.derivative ((normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm (z + w))) =
        normalForm zeroDerivation
            (Polynomial.derivative ((normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm z)) +
          normalForm zeroDerivation
            (Polynomial.derivative ((normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm w))
    rw [h, Polynomial.derivative_add, normalForm_add]
  leibniz' := by
    intro z w
    rcases normalForm_surjective zeroDerivation z with ⟨p, rfl⟩
    rcases normalForm_surjective zeroDerivation w with ⟨q, rfl⟩
    rw [← normalForm_mul_zeroDerivation]
    change normalForm zeroDerivation
      (Polynomial.derivative ((normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm
        (normalForm zeroDerivation (p * q)))) =
      normalForm zeroDerivation p *
          normalForm zeroDerivation
            (Polynomial.derivative ((normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm
              (normalForm zeroDerivation q))) +
        normalForm zeroDerivation
            (Polynomial.derivative ((normalFormAddEquiv zeroDerivation).symm
              (normalForm zeroDerivation p))) *
          normalForm zeroDerivation q
    rw [normalFormAddEquiv_symm_normalForm,
      normalFormAddEquiv_symm_normalForm, normalFormAddEquiv_symm_normalForm]
    rw [Polynomial.derivative_mul, normalForm_add,
      normalForm_mul_zeroDerivation, normalForm_mul_zeroDerivation]
    exact add_comm _ _

/-- The quotient presentation is canonically equivalent to the recursive
Ore construction, without using PBW independence for the quotient. -/
def presentedIteratedEquiv (n : Nat) :
    PresentedWeyl k n ≃ₐ[k] IteratedPairStage k n :=
  AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom (presentedToIterated k n) (iteratedToPresented k n)
    (presentedToIterated_comp_iteratedToPresented k n)

Stafford38.WeylIteratedEquivalence.iteratedToPresented Lean onlyStafford38/Weyl/IteratedEquivalence.lean:441
/-- The recursive map from the Ore tower back to the quotient presentation. -/
def iteratedToPresented :
    (n : Nat) → IteratedPairStage k n →ₐ[k] PresentedWeyl k n
  | 0 => Algebra.ofId k (PresentedWeyl k 0)
  | n + 1 => by
      letI : Algebra k (IteratedPairStage k n) :=
        iteratedPairStageAlgebra k n
      letI : Algebra k (PairStage (B := IteratedPairStage k n)) :=
        pairStageAlgebra
      change PairStage (B := IteratedPairStage k n) →ₐ[k]
        PresentedWeyl k (n + 1)
      let f : IteratedPairStage k n →ₐ[k] PresentedWeyl k (n + 1) :=
        (previousWeylEmbedding k n).comp (iteratedToPresented n)
      exact pairLiftAlgHom f (presentedCoordinate k n) (presentedMomentum k n)
        (fun b => presentedCoordinate_commutes_previous k n
          (iteratedToPresented n b))
        (fun b => presentedMomentum_commutes_previous k n
          (iteratedToPresented n b))
        (presentedMomentum_mul_coordinate k n)

tower. -/

Definition 2.4 ([Coutinho 1995, Ch. 8.3]).

A filtration of a right AnA_nAn​-module MMM compatible with a filtration F∙F_\bulletF∙​ is an exhaustive increasing chain of kkk-subspaces M∙M_\bulletM∙​ with MiFj⊆Mi+jM_iF_j\subseteq M_{i+j}Mi​Fj​⊆Mi+j​ and Mi=0M_i=0Mi​=0 for i<0i<0i<0. The associated graded module is gr⁡M=⨁iMi/Mi−1\operatorname{gr}M=\bigoplus_iM_i/M_{i-1}grM=⨁i​Mi​/Mi−1​; it is a graded module over gr⁡FAn(k)\operatorname{gr}_FA_n(k)grF​An​(k) via the maps Mi/Mi−1×Fj/Fj−1→Mi+j/Mi+j−1M_i/M_{i-1}\times F_j/F_{j-1}\to M_{i+j}/M_{i+j-1}Mi​/Mi−1​×Fj​/Fj−1​→Mi+j​/Mi+j−1​, (mˉ,aˉ)↦ma‾(\bar m,\bar a)\mapsto\overline{ma}(mˉ,aˉ)↦ma, which are well defined because Mi−1Fj⊆Mi+j−1M_{i-1}F_j\subseteq M_{i+j-1}Mi−1​Fj​⊆Mi+j−1​ and MiFj−1⊆Mi+j−1M_iF_{j-1}\subseteq M_{i+j-1}Mi​Fj−1​⊆Mi+j−1​. It is good if the associated graded module is finitely generated over gr⁡FAn\gr^FA_ngrFAn​.

Stafford38.Paper.Section2.IsCompatibleFiltration structureStafford38/Paper/Section2/Filtration.lean:198
/-- **Definition 2.4 (compatible filtration).** An exhaustive increasing chain
`M_0 ⊆ M_1 ⊆ …` of `k`-subspaces (`M_i = 0` for `i < 0`) with
`M_i F_j ⊆ M_{i+j}`. -/
structure IsCompatibleFiltration (F : ℕ → Submodule k A) (Mf : ℕ → Submodule k M) :
    Prop where
  mono : Monotone Mf
  smul_mem : ∀ {i j : ℕ} {m : M} {a : A}, m ∈ Mf i → a ∈ F j →
    MulOpposite.op a • m ∈ Mf (i + j)
  exhaustive : ∀ m : M, ∃ i, m ∈ Mf i
Stafford38.Paper.Section2.IsGoodFiltration structureStafford38/Paper/Section2/CharacteristicVariety.lean:44
/-- **Definition 2.4 (good filtration).** A filtration `M_•` of a right
`A_n(k)`-module `M`, compatible with the order filtration `F_•`, is good if
`gr M = ⊕_i M_i/M_{i-1}` is finitely generated over `gr^F A_n = k[x, ξ]`. -/
structure IsGoodFiltration (Γ : ℕ → Submodule k M) : Prop where
  compatible : IsCompatibleFiltration (orderFiltration k n) Γ
  finite : Module.Finite (SymbolRing k n) (GrModule Γ)

/-- **Definition 2.4, example: goodness.** `gr Q` is finitely generated over
`gr A_n = k[x, ξ]`, being generated by `q̄`. -/
theorem grCyclic_good {n : ℕ} (I : RightIdeal (PresentedWeyl k n)) :
    Module.Finite (SymbolRing k n) (grCyclic k I) := by
  refine ⟨⟨{qBar k I}, eq_top_iff.mpr fun m _ => ?_⟩⟩
  obtain ⟨f, rfl⟩ := grCyclic_generated k I m
  exact Submodule.smul_mem _ f (Submodule.subset_span (by simp))

  map_smul' c a := show MulOpposite.op (c • a) • q = c • (MulOpposite.op a • q) by

the set of points at which all elements of JJJ vanish; these sets are the (Zariski) closed sets of the Zariski topology on Spec⁡S\operatorname{Spec}SSpecS. For a field KKK and an ideal J⊆K[z1,…,zN]J\subseteq K[z_1,\dots,z_N]J⊆K[z1​,…,zN​] we write

for its (classical) zero set, and for S⊆KNS\subseteq K^NS⊆KN we write I(S)={f∈K[z]:f(a)=0 ∀a∈S}I(S)=\{f\in K[z]: f(a)=0\ \forall a\in S\}I(S)={f∈K[z]:f(a)=0 ∀a∈S} for the vanishing ideal of SSS. The sets VK(J)V_K(J)VK​(J) are the closed sets of the Zariski topology on KNK^NKN. /-- **Definition 2.6, last sentence.** `a ∈ V_K(J)` iff `𝔪_a ∈ V(J)`. -/
theorem mem_VK_iff_closedPoint_mem_V (J : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) (a : σ → K) :
    a ∈ VK K J ↔ closedPoint K a ∈ V J := by
  rw [mem_V_iff]
  change (∀ f ∈ J, MvPolynomial.eval a f = 0) ↔ J ≤ maxIdealAt K a
  exact ⟨fun h f hf => (mem_maxIdealAt_iff K a f).mpr (h f hf),
    fun h f hf => (mem_maxIdealAt_iff K a f).mp (h hf)⟩

  ⟨maxIdealAt K a, Ideal.IsMaximal.isPrime inferInstance⟩

theorem definition_2_7_independent {Γ Γ' : ℕ → Submodule k M}
    (hΓ : IsGoodFiltration k n Γ) (hΓ' : IsGoodFiltration k n Γ') :
    CharOf k n Γ = CharOf k n Γ' := by
  rw [CharOf, CharOf, V, V, ← PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_radical,
    radical_annihilator_eq_of_good hΓ.compatible hΓ'.compatible hΓ.finite hΓ'.finite,
    PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_radical]

Definition 2.8 ([Hotta 2008, Ch. E.1]).

A bilinear form ω\omegaω on a kkk-vector space is symplectic if it is antisymmetric and nondegenerate. The standard symplectic form on k2nk^{2n}k2n with basis x1,…,xn,∂1,…,∂nx_1,\dots,x_n,\partial_1,\dots,\partial_nx1​,…,xn​,∂1​,…,∂n​ is determined by

ω(xi,∂j)=δij,ω(xi,xj)=ω(∂i,∂j)=0, \omega(x_i,\partial_j)=\delta_{ij},\qquad \omega(x_i,x_j)=\omega(\partial_i,\partial_j)=0,ω(xi​,∂j​)=δij​,ω(xi​,xj​)=ω(∂i​,∂j​)=0,
analogously to the Weyl relations. Under the correspondence ∂i↔ξi\partial_i\leftrightarrow\xi_i∂i​↔ξi​, on T∗XT^*XT∗X (Definition 2.5) it takes the familiar form ω=∑i=1ndxi∧dξi\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n dx_i\wedge d\xi_iω=∑i=1n​dxi​∧dξi​. /-- **Definition 2.8 (symplectic form).** `ω` is antisymmetric and
nondegenerate (`ω(u, ·) = 0` forces `u = 0`). -/
def IsSymplectic (ω : BilinForm k V) : Prop :=
  (∀ x y, ω x y = -ω y x) ∧ ω.Nondegenerate

def gramMatrix {ι : Type*} (ω : BilinForm k V) (b : ι → V) : Matrix ι ι k :=
  fun i j => ω (b i) (b j)

/-- **Definition 2.8 (symplectic basis).** `e_1, …, e_n, f_1, …, f_n` with
`ω(e_i, f_j) = δ_ij` and `ω(e_i, e_j) = ω(f_i, f_j) = 0`. -/
def IsSymplecticBasis {n : ℕ} (ω : BilinForm k V) (b : Basis (Fin n ⊕ Fin n) k V) :
    Prop :=
  (∀ i j, ω (b (Sum.inl i)) (b (Sum.inr j)) = if i = j then 1 else 0) ∧
    (∀ i j, ω (b (Sum.inl i)) (b (Sum.inl j)) = 0) ∧
    (∀ i j, ω (b (Sum.inr i)) (b (Sum.inr j)) = 0)

/-- **Definition 2.8 (standard symplectic form).** On `𝕍 = k^{2n}` with basis
`x_1, …, x_n, ∂_1, …, ∂_n`, `ω(u, v) = ∑_i (u_{x_i} v_{∂_i} - u_{∂_i} v_{x_i})`,
so `ω(x_i, ∂_j) = δ_ij` and `ω(x_i, x_j) = ω(∂_i, ∂_j) = 0`.  It is the
negative of the repository's `phasePairing`, which uses the opposite sign
convention. -/
def omega (n : ℕ) : BilinForm k (PhaseVar n → k) :=
  LinearMap.mk₂ k (fun u v => -phasePairing k u v)
    (fun u v w => by rw [phasePairing_add_left, neg_add])
    (fun c u v => by rw [phasePairing_smul_left, smul_eq_mul, mul_neg])
    (fun u v w => by rw [phasePairing_add_right, neg_add])
    (fun c u v => by rw [phasePairing_smul_right, smul_eq_mul, mul_neg])

/-- **Definition 2.9 (Poisson bracket).**
`{f, g} = ∑_i (∂f/∂x_i ∂g/∂ξ_i - ∂f/∂ξ_i ∂g/∂x_i)` on `k[x, ξ]`. -/
def poisson {n : ℕ} (f g : SymbolRing k n) : SymbolRing k n :=
  ∑ i : Fin n,
    (MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl i) f * MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inr i) g -
      MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inr i) f * MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl i) g)

/-- **Theorem 2.11 (Gabber).** Let `K` be a field of characteristic zero and `M`
a finitely generated right `A_n(K)`-module with a good order filtration `M_•`
(Definition 2.4, `IsGoodFiltration`: compatible and exhaustive, `gr M` finitely
generated over `K[x, ξ]`).  Then `J = √(Ann_{K[x,ξ]} gr M)` is involutive.  The cited result
[Gab81] is proved in `Stafford38.Paper.Support.Gabber`, by reduction to cyclic
modules and the repository's proof of the cyclic case. -/
theorem theorem_2_11 (K : Type u) [Field K] [CharZero K] (n : ℕ)
    {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module (Stafford38Challenge.WeylAlg K n)ᵐᵒᵖ M] [Module K M]
    [IsScalarTower K (Stafford38Challenge.WeylAlg K n)ᵐᵒᵖ M]
    [Module.Finite (Stafford38Challenge.WeylAlg K n)ᵐᵒᵖ M]
    (Γ : ℕ → Submodule K M) (hgood : IsGoodFiltration K n Γ) :
    IsInvolutive K (Module.annihilator (SymbolRing K n)
      (Stafford38.Paper.Support.Gabber.GrModule Γ)).radical :=
  (isInvolutive_iff K _).2 (Stafford38.Paper.Support.Gabber.theorem_2_11_general K n Γ
    hgood.compatible hgood.finite)

/-- **Theorem 2.12 (Hilbert's Nullstellensatz).** Let `K` be algebraically
closed and `J ⊆ K[z_1, …, z_N]` an ideal (the variables indexed by any
finite type `σ`, e.g. `PhaseVar n` for `K[x, ξ]`).
(a) The maximal ideals of `K[z]` are exactly the `𝔪_a`, `a ↦ 𝔪_a` is
injective, and `V_K(J)` corresponds to the closed points of `V(J)`;
(b) `V_K(J) = ∅` iff `1 ∈ J`;
(c) `I(V_K(J)) = √J`. -/
theorem theorem_2_12 [IsAlgClosed K] [Finite σ] (J : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) :
    ((∀ M : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K), M.IsMaximal ↔ ∃ a, M = maxIdealAt K a) ∧
      Function.Injective (maxIdealAt K (σ := σ)) ∧
      ∀ a, a ∈ VK K J ↔ closedPoint K a ∈ V J) ∧
    (VK K J = ∅ ↔ (1 : MvPolynomial σ K) ∈ J) ∧
    vanishingIdealOf K (VK K J) = J.radical := by
  have hc : vanishingIdealOf K (VK K J) = J.radical := by
    rw [vanishingIdealOf, VK_eq_zeroLocus, MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal_zeroLocus_eq_radical]
  refine ⟨⟨fun M => ?_, ?_, mem_VK_iff_closedPoint_mem_V K J⟩, ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩, hc⟩
  · simp only [maxIdealAt_eq_vanishingIdeal]
    exact MvPolynomial.isMaximal_iff_eq_vanishingIdeal_singleton
  · intro a b hab
    funext i
    have hmem : MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.C (a i) ∈ maxIdealAt K b :=
      hab ▸ Ideal.subset_span ⟨i, rfl⟩
    rw [mem_maxIdealAt_iff] at hmem
    simpa [sub_eq_zero, eq_comm] using hmem
  · have h1 : (1 : MvPolynomial σ K) ∈ J.radical := by
      rw [← hc, h, mem_vanishingIdealOf]
      simp
    exact (Ideal.radical_eq_top.mp ((Ideal.eq_top_iff_one _).mpr h1)).symm ▸ Submodule.mem_top
  · ext a
    simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
    intro ha
    simpa using ha 1 h

Paragraph: consequences without printed proof

formalizesgraph50e662dbac54e441

Left modules are Module A_n(k) M. Finite-order differential operators are k-linear endomorphisms killed by N+1 iterated commutators with multiplications (Grothendieck); "localizations" are all B with IsLocalization S B for a submonoid S of k[x₁,…,xₙ]; Laurent coefficients are the localization at x₁⋯xₙ. In the evolutionary identity k is a field of characteristic zero, the convention of Section 2, and the Lean proof uses neither Theorem 1.1 nor Section 5.

Generalizations and open questions
The formalization in Lean discussed in Section 1.2 also proves the following consequences, which have no printed proof: the left-handed identity 1=Rd+SdF1=Rd+SdF1=Rd+SdF, via the formal adjoint, which implies Corollary 6.3 also for left torsion modules; the identity for finite-order differential operators on localizations of k[x1,…,xn]k[x_1,\dots,x_n]k[x1​,…,xn​], including principal opens, Laurent-polynomial coefficients and the fraction field k(x1,…,xn)k(x_1,\dots,x_n)k(x1​,…,xn​); and, independently of the geometric part of Section 5, the identity with F=xrF=x^rF=xr for d=pr−∑jajxmjd=p^r-\sum_j a_jx^{m_j}d=pr−∑j​aj​xmj​, r≥1r\ge1r≥1, in any kkk-algebra containing elements x,px,px,p with px=xp+1px=xp+1px=xp+1, provided each aja_jaj​ commutes with xxx and ppp. Lean: Stafford38.LocalizationCorollaries.s38_rightOreLocalization; Stafford38.LeftHandedCorollary.leftHanded_of_universalStatement; Stafford38.LocalizedDifferentialCorollaries.s38_unconditional_localized_differential; Stafford38.Evolution.evolutionaryCorollary

/-- **Corollary 6.3 for left torsion modules.** Every finitely generated torsion
left `A_n(k)`-module is cyclic.  The left analogue of the printed proof
(`Section6.corollary_6_3_of` for the ring `A_n(k)ᵐᵒᵖ`, whose right modules are
the left `A_n(k)`-modules), fed with the left-handed identity `1 = Rd + SdF`
(`leftHandedIdentity`) and the left Ore condition; the two generators of the
left version of [Sta78, Thm. 3.7] come from the same identity. -/
theorem corollary_6_3_left : LeftCorollary_6_3.{u, v} := by
  intro k _ _ n M _ _ _ hM
  let ψ : (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖᵐᵒᵖ →+* WeylAlg k n := (RingEquiv.opOp (WeylAlg k n)).symm.toRingHom
  let : Module (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖᵐᵒᵖ M := Module.compHom M ψ
  have hsmul : ∀ (a : WeylAlg k n) (m : M),
      (MulOpposite.op (MulOpposite.op a) : (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖᵐᵒᵖ) • m = a • m := fun _ _ => rfl
  have hone : ∀ d : (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ, d ≠ 0 →
      ∃ F R S : (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ, (1 : (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ) = d * R + F * d * S := by
    intro d hd
    obtain ⟨R, S, F, h⟩ := leftHandedIdentity k n d.unop
      (fun h0 => hd (MulOpposite.unop_injective (by rw [h0, MulOpposite.unop_zero])))
    refine ⟨MulOpposite.op F, MulOpposite.op R, MulOpposite.op S, ?_⟩
    apply MulOpposite.unop_injective
    simp only [MulOpposite.unop_one, MulOpposite.unop_add, MulOpposite.unop_mul,
      MulOpposite.unop_op, h, mul_assoc]
  have : Module.Finite (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖᵐᵒᵖ M := by
    obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (Module.Finite.fg_top : (⊤ : Submodule (WeylAlg k n) M).FG)
    refine ⟨⟨s, ?_⟩⟩
    let N : Submodule (WeylAlg k n) M :=
      { carrier := Submodule.span (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖᵐᵒᵖ (s : Set M)
        add_mem' := fun ha hb => Submodule.add_mem _ ha hb
        zero_mem' := Submodule.zero_mem _
        smul_mem' := fun c x hx => by
          change c • x ∈ Submodule.span (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖᵐᵒᵖ (s : Set M)
          rw [← hsmul]
          exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ hx }
    have hN : (⊤ : Submodule (WeylAlg k n) M) ≤ N := by
      rw [← hs]
      exact Submodule.span_le.2 fun x hx => Submodule.subset_span hx
    exact eq_top_iff.2 fun x _ => hN Submodule.mem_top
  have hT : Stafford38.Paper.Section2.IsTorsion (WeylAlg k n)ᵐᵒᵖ M := by
    intro m
    obtain ⟨d, hd, hdm⟩ := hM m
    refine ⟨MulOpposite.op d, fun h => hd (MulOpposite.op_injective (by rw [h, MulOpposite.op_zero])),
      ?_⟩
    rw [hsmul, hdm]
  have hOre := weyl_leftOreCondition k n
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := (Section6.corollary_6_3_of hOre hone hT
    ⟨Section6.two_generators_of_identity hOre hone hT,
      fun l hl => Section6.stably_generated_of_identity hOre hone hT l (by omega)⟩).1
  refine ⟨m, fun x => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hm x
  exact ⟨a.unop, ha⟩

/-- The identity `1 = dR + FdS` in the ring `D_k(B)` of finite-order
`k`-linear differential operators on `B`: for every nonzero `d ∈ D_k(B)` there
are `F, R, S ∈ D_k(B)` with `1 = dR + FdS`. -/
def HasDifferentialIdentity (k : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing k] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra k B] : Prop :=
  ∀ d : Module.End k B, IsDifferentialOperator k B d → d ≠ 0 →
    ∃ F R S : Module.End k B, IsDifferentialOperator k B F ∧ IsDifferentialOperator k B R ∧
      IsDifferentialOperator k B S ∧ (1 : Module.End k B) = d * R + F * d * S

/-- `P` is a `k`-linear differential operator of finite order on `B`. -/
def IsDifferentialOperator (k : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing k] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra k B] (P : Module.End k B) : Prop :=
  ∃ N, IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrder k B N P
Stafford38Challenge.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrder defStafford38/PaperClaimDefinitions.lean:61
/-- `P` is a `k`-linear differential operator of order at most `N` on the
commutative `k`-algebra `B` (Grothendieck): every iterated commutator
`[…[[P, b₀], b₁], …, b_N]` with multiplication operators vanishes, where
`[Q, b] = Q ∘ b − b ∘ Q`. -/
def IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrder (k : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing k] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra k B] (N : ℕ) (P : Module.End k B) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : List B, b.length = N + 1 →
    b.foldl (fun Q c => Q * LinearMap.mulLeft k c - LinearMap.mulLeft k c * Q) P = 0

The proof of Theorem 1.1 shows Q=0Q=0Q=0 without producing RRR and SSS. Over a computable field, the fixed choice of FFF nevertheless gives a terminating algorithm: enumerate the countably many pairs (g,D)(g,D)(g,D) of linear symplectic changes of generators and degree bounds, and solve the linear system 1=dR+FdS1=dR+FdS1=dR+FdS with F=Φg−1(x1)deg⁡BdF=\Phi_g^{-1}(x_1)^{\deg_Bd}F=Φg−1​(x1​)degB​d for R,SR,SR,S of Bernstein degree at most DDD. Theorem 1.1 guarantees that some pair succeeds. We cannot provide bounds for deg⁡BR\deg_BRdegB​R and deg⁡BS\deg_BSdegB​S in terms of deg⁡Bd\deg_BddegB​d, so the question for an efficient algorithm remains open. History of the work; the mathematical content is Sections 3 to 6.

AI agents assisted with proof discovery, counterexample searches, review, formalization and writing. The work began with computations in Macaulay2 and Maple. Direct attempts to construct universal cofactors produced special cases and reductions, but no general construction. The decisive step was to study the quotient Q=An/(dAn+x1NdAn)Q=A_n/(dA_n+x_1^N dA_n)Q=An​/(dAn​+x1N​dAn​) and to show that its characteristic support is empty.

No Lean counterpart.

Paragraph: paper from Lean

prosegraph48e206fb50eb22e8

Describes how the text was written; this view is where the correspondence it claims can be checked.

The first complete argument was written by AI agents in the style of a paper proof. Agents then formalized it in Lean, and the formalization changed parts of the argument where the original steps could not be checked as written. After the Lean proof was complete and published, the paper proof was rewritten from the checked Lean proof, so that every statement corresponds to a Lean declaration and every difference between the two routes is marked in the text. The authors are reviewing this correspondence and revising the text for clarity together with the agents, until both the human review and the AI checks raise no further objections.

No Lean counterpart.

One controlling agent kept the authoritative state of the proof. Parallel agents worked on separate approaches and returned evidence together with its scope, and independent reviewer agents checked each result before it was accepted. The first author steered the work with short instructions, and the agents wrote the detailed task prompts for each other. Advice from consultations counted only after an independent check.

The working rules developed together with the proof into a reusable agent skill for open mathematical problems. Early versions emphasized falsification and keeping conditional results apart from established ones. Once a candidate proof existed, the emphasis moved to repairing the first invalid step of a promising argument, and to auditing proofs.

Research and review used OpenAI GPT models from GPT-5.5 to GPT-6.1, Anthropic Claude models from Haiku 4.5 to Opus 5, and locally hosted Qwen and DeepSeek models. GPT and Claude models, most recently Claude Opus 5.5, helped draft and revise the manuscript and the supplementary material. The authors are responsible for the final text.

Paragraph: checks

prosegraphe1788ee46b787d2e

Checks of the formal proof by tools outside this view (Comparator, NanoDa, Palomar); not a mathematical claim.

The formal proof uses Lean 4, Mathlib and AlgebraicAnalysis v0.3.3 [Moura 2021, Community 2020, Albert 2026]. Conditional results were kept apart from proved ones until every hypothesis was discharged. Comparator checked that the proved theorems have exactly the statements of separate challenge files that use only Mathlib definitions, and both the Lean kernel and the independent checker NanoDa accepted the proofs [contributors, NanoDa, Registry]. Theorem 1.1 and generalization (a) of Section 7 are registered in the Palomar registry [Albert 2026, Albert 2026], and their Lean sources are archived [Albert, Albert 2026].

No Lean counterpart.
